Putting forward long-term solutions to flood control, Manila City Mayor @IskoMoreno urged the national government to build more sewage treatment plants or STPs in the nation's capital.

In a radio interview, Domagoso said building more STPs will give the city a strong capability to prevent flooding despite heavy rainfall, as opposed to short-term measures of weekly declogging. 

But right now, in the absence of STPs, the Mayor said the city will have to continue holding the line by strictly and consistently conducting declogging operations. 

“The long-term solution is to create more STPs," Domagoso said. "Dinagdagan mo ’yung load ng tubig na maibato sa dagat, na kailangan malinis.” 

In putting forward this long-term solution, the Mayor referred to a Supreme Court writ of continuing mandamus which required national government agencies to clean up, rehabilitate, and preserve Manila Bay, including the installation and operation of adequate sewage treatment facilities.

Domagoso explained that the construction of sewage treatment plants under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) was necessary to comply with the court ruling.

However, he noted that existing STPs are insufficient to handle the volume of water entering the city during heavy rains.

“Sa Roxas Boulevard, ’yung pagsunod ng ating estado sa kautusan ng Supreme Court, ginawa at gumawa ang DENR, DPWH ng what you call STP (Sewage Treatment Plant). Maganda po ’yun, ’yun po ang solusyon sa pagtupad sa mandamus ruling o requirements ng estado na galing sa Supreme Court," Domagoso said. 

"Kaya lamang, ’yung mga tubo, kasi binarahan ang mga main canal natin, tatlo o apat na kanal na malalaki, ’yung tubo po ay hindi na sumasapat sa paghigop sa dami na at bilis ng daluyong ng tubig at ulan o baha,” he noted. 

The Mayor also stressed that more STPs should not be limited to Roxas Boulevard, where most existing facilities are located, but should also be built in other flood-prone areas. 

“But not Roxas Boulevard alone, because Manila Bay, if we are going to follow mandamus, kailangan po pati sa Baseco, sa 105, sa 128, sa Parola, those are the areas na may papuntang tubig sa lupa papuntang dagat,” he said.

He also shared that an inspection of Manila’s drainage system during the recent heavy rains revealed that some streets flooded due to clogged inlets filled with sand, soil, and silt—not garbage—suggesting that proper maintenance could also reduce flooding. 

He added that some newly built pumping stations had yet to become operational, which worsened flooding in several areas, including Taft Avenue. 

“Ang tingin po namin, ’yung mga bagong pumping stations na hindi pa tangan ng MMDA. Ibig sabihin, hindi pa ho naibigay sa kanila ang puder, hindi po gumagana," Domagoso said.

"Kasi ang mga pumping station naman ng aming syudad na sa pangangalaga ng MMDA, tumatakbo naman po halos lahat. Pero ’yung mga bagong ipinagawa, it’s either brand new and non-operational, unusable and defective. That’s the truth of the matter,” he added.

Tingog Partylist Rep. Yedda Romualdez and Community Engagement Director Karla Estrada led relief operations in flood-stricken areas of Metro Manila amid heavy rains brought by Severe Tropical Storm Crising and the intensified southwest monsoon.

As Tropical Depression Dante threatens parts of the country, Tingog Partylist urged the public to remain vigilant and heed official advisories.

BAM SEEKS PROBE INTO ₱360-B FLOOD CONTROL BUDGET AMID WIDESPREAD FLOODING

Sen. Bam Aquino has called for an extensive Senate investigation into the government's flood control programs following days of torrential rain that left many areas across the country submerged.

Aquino raised concerns over the persistent flooding despite the allocation of billions in public funds. Under the proposed 2025 national budget, around ₱360 billion—or nearly 20 percent of the ₱1.6-trillion infrastructure budget—has been earmarked for flood control under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) and other agencies.

"Flood control ang pangako, pero flood out of control ang inabot ng taumbayan. Kailangang busisiin natin nang husto kung nagamit ba sa tama ang bilyun-bilyong pisong pondo para sa flood control," Aquino said.

He also questioned the effectiveness of current flood mitigation plans and urged a review to ensure taxpayers' money is not wasted. "Mabuti ring alamin kung epektibo pa ba ang mga plano natin sa flood control o baka nagsasayang lang at napupunta sa wala ang pera mula sa buwis ng taumbayan," he added.

Aquino emphasized the need to protect communities from the worsening effects of climate change.

The senator has also been actively leading relief operations in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), Angat Buhay, Kaya Natin, Kitchen Stories, and other partner organizations. He visited a soup kitchen in Marikina on Thursday and is scheduled to lead similar efforts in Pampanga today.

Aquino first launched this initiative last year, during Typhoon Carina, while serving as chairman of Kaya Natin.

MMDA to Implement Zipper Lane Along Elliptical corner Commonwealth Ave for PBBM’s 4th SONA on July 28

The Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) will implement a zipper lane or counterflow along Commonwealth Avenue to give way to vehicles of government officials and guests going to the Batasang Pambansa in Quezon City for President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s fourth State of the Nation Address (SONA) on Monday, July 28.

Motorists are advised to take alternate routes to avoid the anticipated heavy traffic along Commonwealth Avenue and IBP Road.

ALTERNATE ROUTES:
NORTHBOUND (Quezon Memorial Circle to Fairview)
• Vehicles from Elliptical Road should take North Avenue, right turn at Mindanao Avenue, then right turn to Sauyo Road, or take Quirino Highway to reach the point of destination.
SOUTHBOUND (Fairview to Quezon Memorial Circle)
• Vehicles from Commonwealth Avenue should take Sauyo Road or Quirino Highway, turn left at Mindanao Avenue, then turn left at North Avenue to reach the point of destination.
FOR LIGHT VEHICLES
• Light vehicles from C5 Road may turn left at Magiting St., turn right at Maginhawa St., turn left at Mayaman St. to Kalayaan Avenue to reach the point of destination.
FOR TRUCKS
• All trucks coming from C-5 along Katipunan Avenue should take the Luzon Flyover then turn left at Congressional Avenue to reach the point of destination.

According to MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes, a total of 1,329 personnel from various units will be deployed to man and manage both vehicular and pedestrian traffic, respond to emergencies, clear roads, and assist in crowd control.

A no-day-off, no-absent policy will be strictly implemented for field traffic personnel.

Ambulances, tow trucks, fire trucks, mobile patrol units, motorcycle units, flood mitigation equipment, and other resources will also be deployed at designated routes and staging areas.

Traffic advisory signage will be put along alternate routes to guide motorists. Plastic barriers and traffic cones will also be installed along zipper lanes and affected roads.

The MMDA Mobile Command Center, equipped with CCTV monitors, will also be stationed at Batasan corner Commonwealth area.

SONA protest actions will be monitored at the MMDA Communications and Command Center located in Pasig City.

The MMDA Special Operations Group-Task Force started conducting road and sidewalk clearing operations in the vicinity of the Batasang Pambansa Complex to ensure that all illegally-parked vehicles and sidewalk vendors were removed so that alternate routes will be fully passable and obstruction-free for motorists.

Motorists are advised to take alternate routes to avoid the anticipated heavy traffic along Commonwealth Avenue and IBP Road.

ALTERNATE ROUTES:
NORTHBOUND (Quezon Memorial Circle to Fairview)
• Vehicles from Elliptical Road should take North Avenue, right turn at Mindanao Avenue, then right turn to Sauyo Road, or take Quirino Highway to reach the point of destination.
SOUTHBOUND (Fairview to Quezon Memorial Circle)
• Vehicles from Commonwealth Avenue should take Sauyo Road or Quirino Highway, turn left at Mindanao Avenue, then turn left at North Avenue to reach the point of destination.
FOR LIGHT VEHICLES
• Light vehicles from C5 Road may turn left at Magiting St., turn right at Maginhawa St., turn left at Mayaman St. to Kalayaan Avenue to reach the point of destination.
FOR TRUCKS
• All trucks coming from C-5 along Katipunan Avenue should take the Luzon Flyover then turn left at Congressional Avenue to reach the point of destination.

According to MMDA Chairman Atty. Don Artes, a total of 1,329 personnel from various units will be deployed to man and manage both vehicular and pedestrian traffic, respond to emergencies, clear roads, and assist in crowd control.

A no-day-off, no-absent policy will be strictly implemented for field traffic personnel.

Ambulances, tow trucks, fire trucks, mobile patrol units, motorcycle units, flood mitigation equipment, and other resources will also be deployed at designated routes and staging areas.

Traffic advisory signage will be put along alternate routes to guide motorists. Plastic barriers and traffic cones will also be installed along zipper lanes and affected roads.

SONA protest actions will be monitored at the MMDA Communications and Command Center located in Pasig City.

Red carpet only for protocol—No pageantry at SONA, says House

ACTING on the request of reelected Leyte Rep. Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez, the House of Representatives has scaled down red carpet activities for this year’s State of the Nation Address (SONA), dropping traditional fashion coverage and ceremonial walk-ins in light of the massive flooding affecting many communities.

Atty. Princess Abante, spokesperson of the House of Representatives, said the changes were outlined in a memorandum issued by House Secretary-General Reginald “Reggie” S. Velasco to all members of the chamber. 

The adjustments, she explained, are meant to demonstrate solidarity with disaster-hit areas and to preserve the solemnity of the national event.

“In view of the recent calamities affecting several regions of the country, the following adjustments will be implemented for the Opening of the 20th Congress and the State of the Nation Address on July 28, 2025,” the July 25 memorandum signed by Velasco said. 

Abante clarified that “the red carpet will still be laid out for official protocol, but it will no longer be a platform for ceremonial arrivals or media spectacle.”

“There will be no staged ceremonies, no fashion coverage, and no photo setups in the red carpet area,” she said.

Only brief doorstop interviews will be allowed, and all media interactions will follow standard security and accreditation procedures.

Formal attire remains required, Abante emphasized, but members are “respectfully urged to avoid ostentatious displays” and to exercise discretion in their wardrobe choices. Barong Tagalog and Filipiniana remain encouraged to reflect the event’s dignity and solemnity.

Based on the memorandum, media access will be limited to accredited personnel and confined to designated areas such as the North and South Wing lobbies and press booths. All activities must strictly comply with House security protocols.

“These adjustments reflect our solidarity with affected communities and our commitment to uphold the dignity of this national gathering,” Velasco wrote.

The move follows an earlier appeal by Rep. Romualdez, who served as Speaker of the 19th Congress, for colleagues and guests to tone down the pageantry in light of the storm damage and prolonged flooding in Luzon and other regions.

He stressed that the House aligns itself with President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s vision of a “Bagong Pilipinas”—a government that puts service, empathy, and accountability above spectacle.

In addition to the protocol changes, the House has also shifted its focus toward disaster response. Under the Ayuda Para sa Kapos ang Kita (AKAP) Program, some P420 million in financial aid has been facilitated for flood victims across 42 districts in Metro Manila and other parts of the country, in line with the President’s directive for immediate assistance.

HOUSE REPS CLOSE RANKS TO BRING AKAP AID TO 42 FLOOD-HIT DISTRICTS – GARIN

Iloilo 1st District Rep. Janette Garin said lawmakers have come together to deliver immediate aid to flood-stricken families in 42 districts across Metro Manila and Rizal through the Ayuda sa Kapos ang Kita Program (AKAP).

Garin said the assistance was made possible through a coordinated push for the mobilization of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), as legislators moved swiftly to help constituents affected by three consecutive typhoons.

The aid effort, she said, was initiated by a core group of House members led by Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez and the Tingog Partylist, and later expanded to include more districts.

"Feeding program, pagbibisita doon sa mga nasa evacuation center… Maybe 42 congressmen, 42 members of the 20th Congress were empowered by using AKAP," Garin said in a media interview.

The program provides financial assistance to low-income earners who lost income due to natural calamities. The expanded list of beneficiaries now includes the districts of Reps. Mia Ynares (Rizal 1st District), Dino Tanjuatco (Rizal 2nd District), Jojo Garcia (Rizal 3rd District), Tom Hernandez (Rizal 4th District), Ronnie Puno (Antipolo 1st District), and Romeo Acop (Antipolo 2nd District).

Garin underscored that lawmakers have no discretion over the final list of recipients, which is prepared and distributed solely by the DSWD.

"The role of the legislators is to call the attention of the DSWD… kung meron dun mga na-exclude because of local or barangay politics. Dapat walang pulitika duon sa implementation sa baba," she said.

Local government units also contribute by providing venues and manpower to ensure safe and efficient distribution, Garin added.

She defended AKAP from critics, arguing that it is a results-oriented program that targets working individuals who are underpaid or whose income is insufficient.

"Dapat hindi ka tamad, dapat nagtatrabaho ka, dapat kulang ang kita mo. Why are we going to stop that?" she said.

Garin called for increased funding for AKAP as Congress enters the 2026 budget season, emphasizing the program's value during disasters.

"We are helping those who are helping themselves," she said.

LEGARDA URGES STRICT ENFORCEMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL LAWS AMID WORSENING FLOODS

Senator Loren Legarda has called for the urgent and strict enforcement of environmental laws, particularly Republic Act No. 9003 or the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act, as severe flooding continues to affect Metro Manila and other parts of the country due to the southwest monsoon.

"We are drowning in our own waste and garbage," said Legarda, principal author of RA 9003, as she pointed to clogged waterways and poor waste management as key contributors to recurring floods.

She warned that the failure to comply with solid waste laws and the continued environmental neglect pose serious threats to communities, especially during heavy rains. "Flooding is not just a matter of inconvenience; it puts our families, our children, our neighbors, and our kababayans' lives at risk. We cannot expect safe, clean, and flood-free communities if we continue to disregard basic environmental rules," she added.

Legarda also cited illegal structures on waterways and weak enforcement at the community level as factors that worsen flooding. "Marami sa mga daluyan ng tubig, kanal, estero, at maging mga ilog ay tinayuan ng bahay, gusali, at istrukturang gawa sa semento at aspalto," she said. "Patuloy tayong nalulubog dahil din sa ating kapabayaan."

She called on local government units, the MMDA, and national agencies to intensify the rehabilitation of esteros and flood-prone areas, and urged citizens to actively participate in barangay cleanup drives. "Flood management is not just a government responsibility. As citizens, we also have to do our part," she said.

Legarda also appealed to the maritime sector to stop dumping waste into the sea, saying monsoon currents carry marine litter to coastal communities. "Our seas, oceans, and rivers are waters that sustain life—they are not trash bins," she said.

As a longtime environmental advocate, Legarda reiterated that flooding and extreme weather events are worsening due to the climate crisis. She is the principal author of the Climate Change Act of 2009 and recently chaired a high-level meeting of the Climate Vulnerable Forum, where she called on global leaders to ramp up climate finance and resilience efforts.

Legarda said environmental protection remains key to disaster preparedness and sustainable development.

Putting forward long-term solutions to flood control, Manila City Mayor @IskoMoreno urged the national government to build more sewage treatment plants or STPs in the nation's capital.

In a radio interview, Domagoso said building more STPs will give the city a strong capability to prevent flooding despite heavy rainfall, as opposed to short-term measures of weekly declogging. 

But right now, in the absence of STPs, the Mayor said the city will have to continue holding the line by strictly and consistently conducting declogging operations. 

“The long-term solution is to create more STPs," Domagoso said. "Dinagdagan mo ’yung load ng tubig na maibato sa dagat, na kailangan malinis.” 

In putting forward this long-term solution, the Mayor referred to a Supreme Court writ of continuing mandamus which required national government agencies to clean up, rehabilitate, and preserve Manila Bay, including the installation and operation of adequate sewage treatment facilities.

Domagoso explained that the construction of sewage treatment plants under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) was necessary to comply with the court ruling.

However, he noted that existing STPs are insufficient to handle the volume of water entering the city during heavy rains.

“Sa Roxas Boulevard, ’yung pagsunod ng ating estado sa kautusan ng Supreme Court, ginawa at gumawa ang DENR, DPWH ng what you call STP (Sewage Treatment Plant). Maganda po ’yun, ’yun po ang solusyon sa pagtupad sa mandamus ruling o requirements ng estado na galing sa Supreme Court," Domagoso said. 

"Kaya lamang, ’yung mga tubo, kasi binarahan ang mga main canal natin, tatlo o apat na kanal na malalaki, ’yung tubo po ay hindi na sumasapat sa paghigop sa dami na at bilis ng daluyong ng tubig at ulan o baha,” he noted. 

The Mayor also stressed that more STPs should not be limited to Roxas Boulevard, where most existing facilities are located, but should also be built in other flood-prone areas. 

“But not Roxas Boulevard alone, because Manila Bay, if we are going to follow mandamus, kailangan po pati sa Baseco, sa 105, sa 128, sa Parola, those are the areas na may papuntang tubig sa lupa papuntang dagat,” he said.

He also shared that an inspection of Manila’s drainage system during the recent heavy rains revealed that some streets flooded due to clogged inlets filled with sand, soil, and silt—not garbage—suggesting that proper maintenance could also reduce flooding. 

He added that some newly built pumping stations had yet to become operational, which worsened flooding in several areas, including Taft Avenue. 

“Ang tingin po namin, ’yung mga bagong pumping stations na hindi pa tangan ng MMDA. Ibig sabihin, hindi pa ho naibigay sa kanila ang puder, hindi po gumagana," Domagoso said.

HOUSE REPS CLOSE RANKS TO BRING AKAP AID TO 42 FLOOD-HIT DISTRICTS – GARIN

Iloilo 1st District Rep. Janette Garin said lawmakers have come together to deliver immediate aid to flood-stricken families in 42 districts across Metro Manila and Rizal through the Ayuda sa Kapos ang Kita Program (AKAP).

Garin said the assistance was made possible through a coordinated push for the mobilization of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), as legislators moved swiftly to help constituents affected by three consecutive typhoons.

The aid effort, she said, was initiated by a core group of House members led by Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez and the Tingog Partylist, and later expanded to include more districts.

"Feeding program, pagbibisita doon sa mga nasa evacuation center… Maybe 42 congressmen, 42 members of the 20th Congress were empowered by using AKAP," Garin said in a media interview.

The program provides financial assistance to low-income earners who lost income due to natural calamities. The expanded list of beneficiaries now includes the districts of Reps. Mia Ynares (Rizal 1st District), Dino Tanjuatco (Rizal 2nd District), Jojo Garcia (Rizal 3rd District), Tom Hernandez (Rizal 4th District), Ronnie Puno (Antipolo 1st District), and Romeo Acop (Antipolo 2nd District).

Garin underscored that lawmakers have no discretion over the final list of recipients, which is prepared and distributed solely by the DSWD.

"The role of the legislators is to call the attention of the DSWD… kung meron dun mga na-exclude because of local or barangay politics. Dapat walang pulitika duon sa implementation sa baba," she said.

Local government units also contribute by providing venues and manpower to ensure safe and efficient distribution, Garin added.

She defended AKAP from critics, arguing that it is a results-oriented program that targets working individuals who are underpaid or whose income is insufficient.

"Dapat hindi ka tamad, dapat nagtatrabaho ka, dapat kulang ang kita mo. Why are we going to stop that?" she said.

Garin called for increased funding for AKAP as Congress enters the 2026 budget season, emphasizing the program's value during disasters.

"We are helping those who are helping themselves," she said.

YEDDA, KARLA ESTRADA LEAD TINGOG'S ROLL OUT OF RELIEF OPERATIONS FOR FLOOD-HIT FAMILIES IN METRO MANILA

Tingog Partylist Rep. Yedda Romualdez and Community Engagement Director Karla Estrada led relief operations in flood-stricken areas of Metro Manila amid heavy rains brought by Severe Tropical Storm Crising and the intensified southwest monsoon.

In coordination with the Office of Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez, Tingog delivered relief packs containing rice, water, food, and blankets to 925 families (or 2,490 individuals) in Barangays Sta. Lucia and San Bartolome, Novaliches, Quezon City. The effort was carried out in partnership with Quezon City 5th District Rep. PM Vargas.

Tingog also conducted a feeding program for evacuees in flood-hit Malanday, Marikina City on July 21, where over 4,000 residents were reported to have sought temporary shelter. On the same day, the group extended food aid to fire and flood victims in Nagtahan, Manila.

As Tropical Depression Dante threatens parts of the country, Tingog Partylist urged the public to remain vigilant and heed official advisories.

BAM SEEKS PROBE INTO ₱360-B FLOOD CONTROL BUDGET AMID WIDESPREAD FLOODING

Sen. Bam Aquino has called for an extensive Senate investigation into the government's flood control programs following days of torrential rain that left many areas across the country submerged.

Aquino raised concerns over the persistent flooding despite the allocation of billions in public funds. Under the proposed 2025 national budget, around ₱360 billion—or nearly 20 percent of the ₱1.6-trillion infrastructure budget—has been earmarked for flood control under the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) and other agencies.

"Flood control ang pangako, pero flood out of control ang inabot ng taumbayan. Kailangang busisiin natin nang husto kung nagamit ba sa tama ang bilyun-bilyong pisong pondo para sa flood control," Aquino said.

He also questioned the effectiveness of current flood mitigation plans and urged a review to ensure taxpayers' money is not wasted. "Mabuti ring alamin kung epektibo pa ba ang mga plano natin sa flood control o baka nagsasayang lang at napupunta sa wala ang pera mula sa buwis ng taumbayan," he added.

Aquino emphasized the need to protect communities from the worsening effects of climate change.

The senator has also been actively leading relief operations in coordination with the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), Angat Buhay, Kaya Natin, Kitchen Stories, and other partner organizations. He visited a soup kitchen in Marikina on Thursday and is scheduled to lead similar efforts in Pampanga today.

Aquino first launched this initiative last year, during Typhoon Carina, while serving as chairman of Kaya Natin.

MARCOS ORDERS AGENCIES TO INTENSIFY FLOOD MITIGATION EFFORTS NATIONWIDE

President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has directed government agencies to ramp up flood mitigation efforts across the country as part of a broader push to strengthen disaster resilience and safeguard communities.

In a Palace briefing on Thursday, Presidential Communications Undersecretary and Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the President instructed the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) to ensure that all pumping stations and floodgates are operating at full capacity, and to continue clearing obstructions from waterways.

The President also ordered the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) to update its flood control and drainage master plans, covering Metro Manila, 18 major river basins, and other critical rivers. Both the MMDA and DPWH were likewise tasked with accelerating the update of the Comprehensive Drainage Master Plan to enhance long-term flood risk management.

Castro said Marcos also urged the public to participate in efforts to keep esteros and other waterways clean, emphasizing that disaster prevention is a shared responsibility.

"Lagi pong tandaan: Ang lahat ay dapat na nagtutulungan upang maiwasan ang anumang sakuna dahil sa Bagong Pilipinas, bawat buhay ay mahalaga at ang bawat isa ay may bilang," Castro said.

Why Filipinos keep getting married in flooded churches

In the Philippines, viral images of couples marrying in flooded churches have drawn admiration for their perseverance, but they also highlight a troubling pattern. Most recently, Jamaica Aguilar and Jade Rick Verdillo tied the knot at Barasoain Church   while standing knee-deep in rainwater. The historic church, located north of Manila, was flooded due to intense seasonal monsoons and Typhoon Wipha. Still, the couple chose to go through with the ceremony, saying they wanted to focus on love, not the water.

This isn’t an isolated event. Similar scenes occurred at the same church in past years, turning these soggy weddings into symbols of Filipino resilience. But beneath the romantic optics lies a recurring issue   a flood crisis that continues to disrupt lives, ceremonies, and even funerals.

After exchanging vows, the newlyweds took doxycycline   an antibiotic used to prevent waterborne diseases like leptospirosis. The same day, the church hosted a funeral amid the floodwaters, with a casket placed on stilts. Meanwhile, tens of thousands of Filipinos have been displaced by the rains, and six people have died. As more cyclones loom this month, many are left wondering when the cycle of flooding   and adapting to it   will end.

Putting forward long-term solutions to flood control, Manila City Mayor @IskoMoreno urged the national government to build more sewage treatment plants or STPs in the nation's capital.

In a radio interview, Domagoso said building more STPs will give the city a strong capability to prevent flooding despite heavy rainfall, as opposed to short-term measures of weekly declogging. 

But right now, in the absence of STPs, the Mayor said the city will have to continue holding the line by strictly and consistently conducting declogging operations. 

“The long-term solution is to create more STPs," Domagoso said. "Dinagdagan mo ’yung load ng tubig na maibato sa dagat, na kailangan malinis.” 

In putting forward this long-term solution, the Mayor referred to a Supreme Court writ of continuing mandamus which required national government agencies to clean up, rehabilitate, and preserve Manila Bay, including the installation and operation of adequate sewage treatment facilities.

Domagoso explained that the construction of sewage treatment plants under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) was necessary to comply with the court ruling.

However, he noted that existing STPs are insufficient to handle the volume of water entering the city during heavy rains.

“Sa Roxas Boulevard, ’yung pagsunod ng ating estado sa kautusan ng Supreme Court, ginawa at gumawa ang DENR, DPWH ng what you call STP (Sewage Treatment Plant). Maganda po ’yun, ’yun po ang solusyon sa pagtupad sa mandamus ruling o requirements ng estado na galing sa Supreme Court," Domagoso said. 

"Kaya lamang, ’yung mga tubo, kasi binarahan ang mga main canal natin, tatlo o apat na kanal na malalaki, ’yung tubo po ay hindi na sumasapat sa paghigop sa dami na at bilis ng daluyong ng tubig at ulan o baha,” he noted. 

The Mayor also stressed that more STPs should not be limited to Roxas Boulevard, where most existing facilities are located, but should also be built in other flood-prone areas. 

“But not Roxas Boulevard alone, because Manila Bay, if we are going to follow mandamus, kailangan po pati sa Baseco, sa 105, sa 128, sa Parola, those are the areas na may papuntang tubig sa lupa papuntang dagat,” he said.

He also shared that an inspection of Manila’s drainage system during the recent heavy rains revealed that some streets flooded due to clogged inlets filled with sand, soil, and silt—not garbage—suggesting that proper maintenance could also reduce flooding. 

He added that some newly built pumping stations had yet to become operational, which worsened flooding in several areas, including Taft Avenue. 

“Ang tingin po namin, ’yung mga bagong pumping stations na hindi pa tangan ng MMDA. Ibig sabihin, hindi pa ho naibigay sa kanila ang puder, hindi po gumagana," Domagoso said.

"Kasi ang mga pumping station naman ng aming syudad na sa pangangalaga ng MMDA, tumatakbo naman po halos lahat. Pero ’yung mga bagong ipinagawa, it’s either brand new and non-operational, unusable and defective. That’s the truth of the matter,” he added.

And Manila in its natural state is a flood plain. No amount of drainage will change that.

Reclamation is another cause of flooding along with the natural waterways being paved over.

But there was no trucks to transport goods yet then so the barges going up the Pasig River were the main mode of transport. 

The culprits now are lack of urban planning and adequate flood control systems plus the indiscriminate dumping of garbage by squatters who built houses along the waterways to serve as their toilets.

Putting forward long-term solutions to flood control, Manila City Mayor @IskoMoreno urged the national government to build more sewage treatment plants or STPs in the nation's capital.

In a radio interview, Domagoso said building more STPs will give the city a strong capability to prevent flooding despite heavy rainfall, as opposed to short-term measures of weekly declogging. 

But right now, in the absence of STPs, the Mayor said the city will have to continue holding the line by strictly and consistently conducting declogging operations. 

“The long-term solution is to create more STPs," Domagoso said. "Dinagdagan mo ’yung load ng tubig na maibato sa dagat, na kailangan malinis.” 

In putting forward this long-term solution, the Mayor referred to a Supreme Court writ of continuing mandamus which required national government agencies to clean up, rehabilitate, and preserve Manila Bay, including the installation and operation of adequate sewage treatment facilities.

Domagoso explained that the construction of sewage treatment plants under the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) and the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) was necessary to comply with the court ruling.

However, he noted that existing STPs are insufficient to handle the volume of water entering the city during heavy rains.

“Sa Roxas Boulevard, ’yung pagsunod ng ating estado sa kautusan ng Supreme Court, ginawa at gumawa ang DENR, DPWH ng what you call STP (Sewage Treatment Plant). Maganda po ’yun, ’yun po ang solusyon sa pagtupad sa mandamus ruling o requirements ng estado na galing sa Supreme Court," Domagoso said. 

"Kaya lamang, ’yung mga tubo, kasi binarahan ang mga main canal natin, tatlo o apat na kanal na malalaki, ’yung tubo po ay hindi na sumasapat sa paghigop sa dami na at bilis ng daluyong ng tubig at ulan o baha,” he noted. 

The Mayor also stressed that more STPs should not be limited to Roxas Boulevard, where most existing facilities are located, but should also be built in other flood-prone areas. 

“But not Roxas Boulevard alone, because Manila Bay, if we are going to follow mandamus, kailangan po pati sa Baseco, sa 105, sa 128, sa Parola, those are the areas na may papuntang tubig sa lupa papuntang dagat,” he said.

He also shared that an inspection of Manila’s drainage system during the recent heavy rains revealed that some streets flooded due to clogged inlets filled with sand, soil, and silt—not garbage—suggesting that proper maintenance could also reduce flooding. 

He added that some newly built pumping stations had yet to become operational, which worsened flooding in several areas, including Taft Avenue. 

“Ang tingin po namin, ’yung mga bagong pumping stations na hindi pa tangan ng MMDA. Ibig sabihin, hindi pa ho naibigay sa kanila ang puder, hindi po gumagana," Domagoso said.

"Kasi ang mga pumping station naman ng aming syudad na sa pangangalaga ng MMDA, tumatakbo naman po halos lahat. Pero ’yung mga bagong ipinagawa, it’s either brand new and non-operational, unusable and defective. That’s the truth of the matter,” he added.

DENR: BEFORE YOU BLAME MANILA DOLOMITE BEACH FOR FLOOD…

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has urged a science-based approach to addressing Metro Manila’s persistent flooding issues, following claims from the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) that the Manila Baywalk Dolomite Beach may be contributing to flood problems.

In a statement released Thursday, July 18, 2025, the DENR emphasized that solutions to flooding must be rooted in climate science and hydrological data, citing increased rainfall over the past decade as a major factor in overwhelming the capital's aging drainage systems.

The MMDA recently pointed to the dolomite beach project—built during the Duterte administration—as having obstructed three key drainage outfalls: Faura, Remedios, and Estero de San Antonio Abad. MMDA Chair Romando Artes noted that water was being rerouted through a sewerage treatment plant which struggles to handle surging volumes during heavy rain.

While DENR did not directly refute MMDA's claims, it acknowledged the concerns and reaffirmed its commitment to collaborating with local governments to improve flood risk management. The agency also called for enhanced urban planning strategies, modernized drainage, better waste management, and restored ecosystems to build climate-resilient communities.

Meanwhile, Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon has filed House Resolution No. 56, urging a congressional probe into the dolomite beach project’s approval, environmental compliance, and whether it worsened flooding in Manila. Ridon criticized the ₱389 million project as a “cosmetic” effort with no real benefit to flood prevention, labeling it “a criminal wastage of public funds.”

Here's a detailed breakdown based on the context of the post you’re interested in (https://t.co/C7vwbZ0LV1) and supporting information:

### Meaning of a Red Warning
- **Severity**: It signifies **serious flooding** is imminent or already occurring in flood-prone areas. This is the most critical alert level, suggesting that water levels may reach or exceed 100% capacity in rivers, leading to widespread inundation.
- **Associated Hazard**: The specific hazard mentioned in the post is "Serious FLOODING in flood-prone areas," particularly affecting Metro Manila, Bataan, and parts of Rizal (Rodriguez, San Mateo, Cainta, Antipolo, Taytay). This implies life-threatening conditions, potential property damage, and disruption of infrastructure.
- **Rainfall Threshold**: While exact rainfall amounts can vary, a Red Warning typically corresponds to heavy rainfall exceeding 15 mm per hour or more, sustained over several hours, as per PAGASA’s guidelines and the EXPLAINER from GMA News Online. This can lead to flash floods or river overflows.
- **Action Required**: Residents are urged to take immediate action, including evacuation from low-lying or coastal areas, as highlighted in the GMA News explainer. The public and Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices are advised to monitor conditions closely and prepare for emergencies.

### Contextual Analysis
- **Current Situation (11:35 PM PST, July 21, 2025)**: Since PST (Pacific Standard Time) is 15 hours behind Philippine time (which is UTC+8), the warning was issued at 2:00 PM local time in the Philippines on July 21, 2025. Given it’s now 2:35 PM local time, the situation is actively unfolding. The Red Warning for Metro Manila, a densely populated urban area, is significant, especially under the Southwest Monsoon (Habagat), which is known to bring prolonged heavy rains from May to September.
- **Historical Context**: Past monsoon events, like the 2023 floods, displaced over 200,000 people (per NDCC reports), and a 2022 study in *Hydrology and Earth System Sciences* noted that 70% of Manila’s flooding is worsened by inadequate drainage. This underscores the Red Warning’s gravity.
- **Weather Conditions**: The PAGASA website forecasts temperatures of 25-29°C with high humidity, suggesting sustained rain, aligning with the monsoon’s peak intensity this time of year.

### Practical Implications
- **For Residents**: If you’re in Metro Manila or the listed areas, expect severe flooding, especially in low-lying zones. Evacuate if advised, secure property, and avoid travel. The next update at 2:00 AM local time (11:00 AM PST) will provide further guidance.
- **For Monitoring**: Check PAGASA’s official site (https://t.co/cc6fyFGpc0) or contact their hotline (8927-1335 or 8927-2877) for real-time updates.

DENR: BEFORE YOU BLAME MANILA DOLOMITE BEACH FOR FLOOD…

The Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR) has urged a science-based approach to addressing Metro Manila’s persistent flooding issues, following claims from the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) that the Manila Baywalk Dolomite Beach may be contributing to flood problems.

In a statement released Thursday, July 18, 2025, the DENR emphasized that solutions to flooding must be rooted in climate science and hydrological data, citing increased rainfall over the past decade as a major factor in overwhelming the capital's aging drainage systems.

The MMDA recently pointed to the dolomite beach project—built during the Duterte administration—as having obstructed three key drainage outfalls: Faura, Remedios, and Estero de San Antonio Abad. MMDA Chair Romando Artes noted that water was being rerouted through a sewerage treatment plant which struggles to handle surging volumes during heavy rain.

While DENR did not directly refute MMDA's claims, it acknowledged the concerns and reaffirmed its commitment to collaborating with local governments to improve flood risk management. The agency also called for enhanced urban planning strategies, modernized drainage, better waste management, and restored ecosystems to build climate-resilient communities.

Meanwhile, Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon has filed House Resolution No. 56, urging a congressional probe into the dolomite beach project’s approval, environmental compliance, and whether it worsened flooding in Manila. Ridon criticized the ₱389 million project as a “cosmetic” effort with no real benefit to flood prevention, labeling it “a criminal wastage of public funds.”

HOUSE REPS CLOSE RANKS TO BRING AKAP AID TO 42 FLOOD-HIT DISTRICTS – GARIN

Iloilo 1st District Rep. Janette Garin said lawmakers have come together to deliver immediate aid to flood-stricken families in 42 districts across Metro Manila and Rizal through the Ayuda sa Kapos ang Kita Program (AKAP).

Garin said the assistance was made possible through a coordinated push for the mobilization of the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD), as legislators moved swiftly to help constituents affected by three consecutive typhoons.

The aid effort, she said, was initiated by a core group of House members led by Leyte 1st District Rep. Martin Romualdez and the Tingog Partylist, and later expanded to include more districts.

"Feeding program, pagbibisita doon sa mga nasa evacuation center… Maybe 42 congressmen, 42 members of the 20th Congress were empowered by using AKAP," Garin said in a media interview.

The program provides financial assistance to low-income earners who lost income due to natural calamities. The expanded list of beneficiaries now includes the districts of Reps. Mia Ynares (Rizal 1st District), Dino Tanjuatco (Rizal 2nd District), Jojo Garcia (Rizal 3rd District), Tom Hernandez (Rizal 4th District), Ronnie Puno (Antipolo 1st District), and Romeo Acop (Antipolo 2nd District).

Garin underscored that lawmakers have no discretion over the final list of recipients, which is prepared and distributed solely by the DSWD.

"The role of the legislators is to call the attention of the DSWD… kung meron dun mga na-exclude because of local or barangay politics. Dapat walang pulitika duon sa implementation sa baba," she said.

Local government units also contribute by providing venues and manpower to ensure safe and efficient distribution, Garin added.

She defended AKAP from critics, arguing that it is a results-oriented program that targets working individuals who are underpaid or whose income is insufficient.

"Dapat hindi ka tamad, dapat nagtatrabaho ka, dapat kulang ang kita mo. Why are we going to stop that?" she said.

Garin called for increased funding for AKAP as Congress enters the 2026 budget season, emphasizing the program's value during disasters.

"We are helping those who are helping themselves," she said.
